text:
On what ray of light, absent love,

did your absence alight? All the nakedness

of your presence shines in my eyes.

Duets of solitude speak through my hands,

full of cold acids

and torn horizons.


I see autumn full of hope

like a spring fallen into evening

in which one star alone

lives in the wandering sky of afternoon.


I love you, love, and I say nothing

to call you. I feel

my eyes ache from not weeping. And I see

that your absence finds me

like the blazing sky

and a sad joy in not using it,

like those days when nothing happens

and the whole house

is uselessly illuminated.


In the ruined bedroom of your absence

trampled twilights revive

their rags, purple with memories.

In the lodging of your absence

I occupy everything, driving nails

into the four walls of absence.


And this closed world

that opens onto the interior of an ancient forest

watches time wither,

light turn to dust, and looks in every direction

without finding the point of departure.


Even if you come tomorrow,

in your absence today I lost some kingdom.


Your body is the country of caresses,

where I, a desolate traveler

—the whole itinerary of my kisses—

pass the autumn so as not to die,

without knowing the worth of your absence

like a diamond hidden in what is saddest.

translation.title: Destroyed Song
translation.editorial_note: The translation retains the poem’s absent beloved, its repeated rooms and walls of absence, and the final diamond image.
